title: Hot-shard eviction and circuit-breaker misfire during cross-region token surge — postmortem
creator: Marco Chen
description: During a sustained token-generation surge in EU-West, a small set of GPU shards became hot and triggered aggressive KV-cache eviction. Evictions increased model cold starts and amplified tail latency, which caused downstream heterogeneous circuit-breakers in North America to trip incorrectly due to skewed observed latencies. The result was an extended SLO degradation spanning two regions with user-facing latency and increased cost from repeat cold-starts and fallback routing.
timeline: 2026-02-14T09:12Z - Spike begins: organic traffic from a large customer batch job started ramping EU-West requests (token/sec ~6x baseline)
2026-02-14T09:18Z - Noticeable tail latency increase in EU-West; first internal alert (p99 > 1.8s) fires
2026-02-14T09:21Z - KV-cache eviction rate on shard-gpu-12 jumps from 0.8% to 37% (observed in runtime metrics)
2026-02-14T09:25Z - NA region sees increased SLO error rate due to downstream routing fallbacks; heterogeneous CBs in NA mark backends degraded
2026-02-14T09:27Z - Automated fallback routing routes traffic to secondary model variants causing capacity contention and a second wave of cache thrashing
2026-02-14T09:40Z - Oncall enables emergency short-circuit to stop cross-region failover and limits token window per user to reduce burstiness
2026-02-14T10:05Z - Traffic engineering applies temporary per-customer rate cap; evictions and tail latency progressively recover
2026-02-14T11:10Z - Full mitigation confirmed; post-incident working group formed to investigate root causes and long-term fixes
impact: User-facing p99 latency increased above SLO for ~1 hour in EU-West with spillover affecting NA routing decisions. Estimated customer-visible requests impacted: ~18K. Cost impact: ~12% uplift in GPU runtime for the hour due to repeated cold starts and fallback traffic. No data loss, but increased error rate (rate-limited fallback responses) and degraded quality for a subset of responses.
root_cause: A combination of uneven request fanout to a small subset of GPU shards (hot-shard) plus an overaggressive KV-cache eviction policy on those shards led to cache churn and cold-start amplification. Circuit-breaker heuristics in other regions treated the latency signals as systemic, triggering failovers that increased cross-region traffic and reinforced the hot-spot pattern.
contributing_factors: Shard allocation algorithm allowed concentration of a high-rate customer on 3 GPUs without sufficient affinity spreading
KV-cache eviction threshold (default LRU window) was tuned for median workloads and did not handle repeated short-lived bursts well
Circuit-breaker thresholds used short windows and did not account for heterogeneous cold-start signals (cache miss vs systemic overload)
Fallback routing lacked hysteresis; rapid oscillation caused repeated cold-starts on secondary pools
Insufficient visibility in alerting to correlate cache-eviction metrics with latency signals across regions
immediate_mitigations: Applied emergency per-customer token rate caps to smooth the incoming burst
Temporarily disabled cross-region automatic failover for affected customers to limit treatment of localized latency as global failure
Increased KV-cache size on the hot shards as a stopgap to reduce eviction rate
Added a short cooldown to the heterogeneous circuit-breakers to require sustained degradation before tripping
long_term_action_items: ENG-34902 - Shard placement changes: implement affinity spreader to avoid high-fanout packing on <=4 GPUs (owner: Aisha Kapoor, due: 2026-03-15)
ENG-34910 - KV-cache policy: introduce burst-aware eviction policy and adaptive windowing; add targeted unit/e2e tests for short-burst scenarios (owner: Rafiq Hussein, due: 2026-03-22)
ENG-34934 - Circuit-breaker tuning: modify heuristics to label latency signals with cache-miss tags and require multi-metric confirmation before failover (owner: Serena Park, due: 2026-03-29)
ENG-34956 - Routing hysteresis: implement cooldown and maximum failover frequency per-customer to prevent oscillation (owner: Maya Alvarez, due: 2026-04-05)
ENG-34980 - Observability: create composite alert that correlates KV eviction rate, cache hit ratio, and regional p99 latency; dashboard and runbook update (owner: Marco Chen, due: 2026-03-08)
ENG-35012 - Chaos tests: add synthetic short-burst tests to CI that emulate token surges and validate circuit-breaker + routing behavior (owner: Devex Team, due: 2026-04-12)
PM-4125 - Customer communication: prepare summary for affected customers with mitigation steps and recommended client-side retry/backoff patterns (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-03-01)
verification_plan: Deploy KV-cache adaptive eviction A/B to 10% of traffic and monitor p99, cache-hit ratio, and eviction rate over 7 days
Run shard placement change in staging with synthetic multi-customer fanout load for 48 hours before canary in production
After circuit-breaker heuristic change, simulate cross-region latency perturbations to ensure failovers only occur with corroborating signals
Publish new alerts/dashboards and perform oncall walkthroughs with runbook updates
